- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is bullish (high sentiment scores) — adjust downward by 1–2% for 1–3 day horizons.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish or neutral (low sentiment scores) — add 1–3% to forecast for 1–5 day horizons.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ above recent peak) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Lagged bias: if true outcome is >10% above forecast at day 1–3, model is underreacting — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- Sentiment-driven momentum: if sentiment >0.75 for 3+ consecutive days, forecast should be 1–2% higher than baseline; if sentiment <0.33, reduce by 0.5–1.5%.
